walkthrough:
**Recall what cis-trans isomers are**

Think of them as stereoisomers, not structural isomers. They have the same molecular formula and the same order of bonding, but a different 3D arrangement around a $C=C$ double bond.

Example: $cis\text{-}but\text{-}2\text{-}ene$ vs $trans\text{-}but\text{-}2\text{-}ene$

**Check statement 1, empirical formula**

Empirical formula is the simplest whole number ratio of atoms, derived from molecular formula. Since P and Q have the same molecular formula, they must have the same empirical formula. So 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2, functional groups**

Functional group depends on connectivity, for example $C=C$, $-OH$, $-COOH$. Because cis-trans isomers have identical connectivity, just flipped in space, the functional groups are unchanged. So 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3, skeletal formula**

Skeletal formula is a drawing of the carbon skeleton. To show cis versus trans you must draw the substituents on the same side in one and on opposite sides in the other. The two drawings cannot be identical, otherwise you could not tell P from Q. So 3 is not the same, it must be different.

options.A: This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all the same. Statements 1 and 2 are correct, but 3 is wrong. If the skeletal drawings were identical you would not be able to represent the cis arrangement in one and the trans arrangement in the other.
options.B: This option claims 1 and 2 only are the same. This is correct. Same molecular formula gives same empirical formula, and same connectivity gives same functional groups, while the skeletal drawings must differ to show the different spatial positions around the double bond.
options.C: This option claims 2 and 3 only are the same. It correctly includes 2 but wrongly includes 3 and wrongly excludes 1. Empirical formula must be the same, and skeletal formula must be different to show cis vs trans.
options.D: This option claims 1 only is the same. It correctly includes 1 but wrongly excludes 2. Functional groups depend on how atoms are connected, and cis-trans isomers have the same connectivity, so functional groups must also be identical.
